title: OPTOMICS: Combining optoacoustic imaging phenotypes and multi-omics to advance diabetes healthcare
summary:
It is known that DM type 2 in early stages can cause changes in the smallest blood vessels (microvasculature) in the skin, blood flow and oxygen saturation. However, better examination methods are needed to recognize and understand these changes in detail. Raster scanning optoacoustic mesoscopy (RSOM) can detect these changes non-invasively.
For this study, the skin of healthy individuals as well as individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus with and without concomitant complications will be measured with RSOM. 
In addition, the clinical RSOM measurements will be correlated with molecular (proteomic, metabolomic) and genetic analysis of blood and urine samples. These measurements will be performed on all participants twice at intervals of approximately 12-15 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group A: Patients with diagnosed diabetes mellitus type II without vascular complications. 
Group B: Patients with diagnosed diabetes mellitus type II with at least one microvascular complication (e.g. neuropathy, nephropathy and retinopathy) without macrovascular complications.
Group C: Patients with diagnosed diabetes mellitus type II with microvascular complications and at least one macrovascular complication (e.g. coronary heart disease, carotid atherosclerosis, peripheral arterial occlusive disease).
Group D: 200 healthy participants
Exclusion criteria:
-Refusal to give consent to participate in the study
-Pregnancy or breastfeeding
-Highly pigmented skin (leads to a strong attenuation of the RSOM signal due to the presence of melanin in the skin)
-Documented or suspected light allergy, light intolerance, contact dermatitis and particularly sensitive skin or dermatological diseases (e.g. psoriasis)
-History of smoking (only in healthy subjects)
-Use of a pacemaker, insulin pump or other implanted electronic devices
-Open or infected wounds at the measurement sites
